children: Mortgage rates surpassed the 7% threshold for the first time since January 2025,
30-year fixed-rate mortgages averaged 7.03% as of September 24, up from 6.95% last week and 6.30% in the same period a year ago.
15-year fixed-rate mortgages averaged 6.42%, up from 6.26% a week ago and 5.49% a year ago.

"Mortgage rates rose to 7.12% last week, the highest level since May 2024, leading to a third consecutive weekly decline in mortgage applications," said Bob Broeksmit, president and CEO of the Mortgage Bankers Association.

"Both purchase and refinance applications were down from a year ago, reflecting the continued impact of higher rates on borrower demand. Refinance activity fell to its slowest pace since February 2025, while prospective homebuyers also remained cautious in the face of higher borrowing costs," said Broeksmit.
"The housing market remains supported by a solid labor market and an economy that is growing at a healthy rate," said Sam Khater, Freddie Mac's chief economist.
